tagline.text: Free street dance spectacle where festival teams from across the country compete in Manila

location.label: Location
location.text: Around the Cultural Center of the Philippines Complex, Metro Manila (near Star City and Aliw Theater); check each year's announcement for the venue

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Check yearly announcements (the May 7–9, 2026 edition was cancelled; June 27–29, 2024)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~1,500 (free admission; per person per day including transport, meals and snacks)

children.text: Aliwan Fiesta is the Philippines' largest festival competition, launched in 2003 by MBC Media Group. Well-known festival teams from across the country compete in Manila with street dances, floats and a queen pageant, and watching is free.

Aliwan Fiesta gathers regional festivals from all over the Philippines in one city and lets them compete. The dances, costumes and drumming of festivals like Sinulog and Dinagyang, which you would normally have to travel to see, can be enjoyed together in Manila, so for travelers with no time to tour many provinces it works like a condensed Philippine festival tour. The organizer is the broadcasting and radio group MBC Media Group (MMG), and according to Wikipedia it has run the event since 2003 together with the Cultural Center of the Philippines (CCP) and the cities of Manila and Pasay. It bills itself as the Philippines' grandest fiesta.

The competition has three main parts. The first and biggest is the Cultural Street Dance Competition, in which each festival team performs a group dance with drums, gongs, feathered headdresses, shields and other props. The second is the Float Parade, where floats must be built from local materials and each carries a queen candidate representing its province. The third is the Reyna ng Aliwan, the Queen of Aliwan pageant. A music contest, Tugtog ng Aliwan, is added on top, so the same team is judged separately on dance, music and costume.

The timing and location change every year, so always check the latest announcement. It reportedly used to be held around Christmas and is now usually held in April or May; in 2024 it took place on June 27–29 at the CCP Complex. The 2025 edition was cancelled because its schedule fell between Holy Week and the May midterm elections, and the 2026 edition planned for May 7–9 was also cancelled, announced by MBC Media Group on March 23, 2026 because of rising fuel costs (the official FAQ page may still show the old schedule). No new date has been confirmed since. For overseas travelers, the safest approach is to check the official website and Facebook announcements before booking flights and accommodation.

Admission is free. The official FAQ says no ticket, advance registration or media pass is needed and anyone can watch. However, it is a crowded outdoor event, so plan your arrival time, the sun and heat, and your ride home in advance.
This is the heart of the event. According to Wikipedia, each of the country's 17 regions may send up to two teams, and in the past the teams paraded along Roxas Boulevard for about
4km
. The number of teams and the parade route differ every year; in 2024, 14 teams took part.

Large floats made from local materials from each province appear. A queen candidate from that province's festival rides on each float and waves to the crowd. In 2024, 8 floats took part, and the Guinakit float from Cotabato City was chosen best float.

This is a pageant in which queen candidates from festivals across the country compete. In 2024, 20 candidates took part and the candidate from Cebu's Pasigarbo sa Sugbo Festival became queen. Ahtisa Manalo, third runner-up at Miss Universe 2025, is also known to have competed in 2017 representing Quezon's Niyogyugan Festival.

According to Wikipedia, Iloilo's Dinagyang Festival has won the most street dance championships, including in 2024. Cebu's Sinulog Festival has the most queen titles. Comparing the two festivals on one stage is a big treat for festival fans.

The competing teams come out in dazzling costumes made of sequins, feathers and beadwork, carrying props such as shields, headdresses and scepters. Even within the Philippines, costume colors and drum rhythms differ greatly from province to province, which makes it a joy for photography.

Wikipedia lists a regional products bazaar as a side event, and the official FAQ also includes instructions for applying for regional bazaar booths. The lineup differs each year, so it is best to see on site which booths appear.

The event is a night event held in the evening over three days. Wikipedia also lists side events such as fireworks and traditional Filipino street games, but they vary by year, so check that year's announcement.

According to the official FAQ, there is a Netizens' Choice Award for which only registered people can vote, limited to twice per day. Even if you cannot attend, you can support your favorite team online.

children.text: Rest at your hotel in central Manila and set out around
. Getting from central Manila to the CCP Complex can take
30 minutes–1 hour
or more depending on traffic, so leave with time to spare.

Arrive near the CCP Complex entrance and check the security line and viewing areas. If you want photos, come early and pick a diagonal spot rather than the front center of the stage for a better view.
Take care of dinner and snacks. Street stalls and food booths sometimes open in and around the venue, so decide on site.

The street dance competition and float parade follow. Each team has a set performance time, so check that day's lineup on the official Facebook page and move to a new spot to catch the teams you want to see.
As the last team wraps up, arrange your ride home. Grab and taxis get swamped at the end of the event, so it is faster to walk toward a nearby main road or large building and book from there.
Start times and order differ every year. The official FAQ says the start time and venue will be announced later.
Watch the opening program and the first competition lineup. This is the day to get a feel for which teams wear which costumes.
This is the day the street dance competition is in full swing. It is a good day to pick your favorite teams and floats and take photos.
The official FAQ says the photographers' area operates on Day 3 on a first-come, first-served basis. The finals and awards atmosphere is the most heated, and the crowd is the largest.
The competition lineup for each day differs every year, so check the official announcements.
The simplest way is to take Grab or a taxi to the CCP Complex from central Manila (Malate, Ermita, Makati).
You can go the same way from the airport (NAIA); depending on the time of day it can take
30 minutes–1 hour
or more.
The CCP Complex is on the Roxas Boulevard waterfront side, so parts of the boulevard may be closed during the event; check the traffic announcements.
The official FAQ only says that traffic notices, alternate routes and road closure information will be posted soon, so no confirmed route can be given.
You can ride LRT-1 to a station close to Roxas Boulevard (toward Gil Puyat or EDSA), get off and transfer to a taxi or Grab.
At going-home hours jeepneys and taxis are crowded, so booking Grab is more reliable late at night.
Decide on the day's routes and closures after checking the announcements.
The official FAQ only says parking locations will be announced separately, so we do not recommend driving your own car.
If you stay at a nearby hotel, you can walk to the venue and avoid the crowds on the way home.

Aliwan Fiesta is not an event with fixed dates; the organizer sets them every year. Wikipedia says it is now usually held in April or May, 2024 was in late June, and the 2026 edition announced for May 7–9 was cancelled.

April and May in the Philippines are the end of the hot dry season, so daytime events call for heat preparation, while June is the start of the rainy season, so prepare for rain. Whichever month it is, the event is held in the evening.

Hotels and restaurants line Roxas Boulevard near the venue, and Malate and Ermita also have plenty of accommodation. Because you may get home late, decide how many of the 3 event days you will attend and then book a hotel close to the CCP Complex to reduce the stress of getting around. The venue may change from year to year, so it is safer to book your accommodation after the location is announced.

You can eat at the food booths and stalls inside the venue, but lines can be long, so having a light meal before you come is also an option. At the provincial festival booths you can sample snacks from places like Iloilo and Cebu, and enjoying the food is part of the fun of this event.

Just before the event, be sure to check the official website (aliwanfiesta.com) and Facebook page for the venue, start time and traffic announcements. The official FAQ says the start time and location will be announced later.
Admission is free and there are no tickets, so do not trust anyone claiming to sell tickets.
It stays muggy even after dark, so bring light clothing, a hat, water and a portable fan.
The official FAQ says the photographers' area is first-come, first-served on Day 3. Unless you are shooting professionally, take photos from the general viewing area.
To avoid the crowd on the way home, leave before the last performance ends or stay somewhere close by.
You can also follow the lineup and team information on radio and TV broadcasts. The official FAQ lists several Facebook pages, regional stations and cable TV coverage.
At the venue, keep your phone and wallet in front of you and watch your belongings.
The venue, dates and parade route change every year, and the event was cancelled in 2025 and 2026, so check the official announcements before settling on flights and accommodation.
The 2025 edition and the 2026 edition (planned for May 7–9) were cancelled. Do not assume it is held every year.
Roads around the venue may be closed, so taxis and Grab may detour or fares may rise.
It is a crowded outdoor event, so beware of pickpockets and lost phones.
Watch out for heat and dehydration, and prepare for sudden showers in the rainy season.
For the parking and first-aid tent locations mentioned in the official FAQ, follow the on-site announcements.

blocks.title: Cultural Center of the Philippines Complex

children.text: A cultural complex where the event is often held. In the daytime it is a nice place to look around the cultural center buildings.
You can watch the sunset along the Roxas Boulevard waterfront. It is good for a walk before or after the event.
A large shopping mall near the venue, convenient for meals or escaping the heat.
The festival of Iloilo, the biggest winner at Aliwan Fiesta. If you want to see the original, visit it on site.
Cebu's signature festival, with many queen titles.
